claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you check your eligibility for Child Benefit! Let me start by getting the first assessment question for you.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking you about your child's age, as this is the first step in determining eligibility.

**How old is your child?**

To help me navigate this correctly, I need to know:
- Is your child **under 16 years old**?
- **16 to 19 years old**? (If so, they may still qualify if in education or training)
- **20 years old or over**?

Also, are you claiming for **one child or multiple children**? If multiple, I'll need to check each one.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who is 3 years old. So yes, under 16. We live together here at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information! That's very helpful. Alex is 3 years old, so definitely under 16. Let me move forward with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to ask you about Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is Alex not in paid work at all?**

(Since Alex is only 3 years old, I'm assuming the answer is "yes" they're not in paid work, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, no - Alex doesn't work at all! He's only 3, so he's not in any kind of paid work.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

(Again, at 3 years old, I'd expect the answer is "yes" they're not receiving these, but I need to confirm.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just 3, so no ESA or Universal Credit or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship, or not in an apprenticeship at all?**

Given that Alex is only 3 years old, I'm expecting the answer is "not in an apprenticeship", but I need to confirm this.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in an apprenticeship - he's only 3! Far too young for that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me move forward.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check your residency situation. This is an important part of the eligibility assessment.

**Can you tell me about where you normally live?**

Here are the main scenarios that would qualify you:

1. **You normally live in the UK** - This is the standard requirement
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme AND** one of the following:
   - You're working and earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months
   - You're actively seeking work (jobseeker for up to 91 days)
   - You have sufficient resources to support yourself and your family financially
   - You're studying and have sufficient resources
   - You're a family member of an EEA or Swiss national with right to reside
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad in certain qualifying countries**

Which of these applies to you? Or could you tell me more about your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live here in the UK - we're in Manchester. I've always lived here, so yes, I normally live in the UK.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's straightforward. You normally live in the UK, so that satisfies the residency requirement. Let me move forward.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex.

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

This means either:
1. **You live with Alex** - which you've already mentioned you do ("We live together here at home")
2. **You're contributing to Alex's upkeep** - paying for food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc.
3. **You're paying maintenance** under a court order or agreement

Since you mentioned you live together at home, I believe you meet the requirement, but can you confirm - you are living with Alex and responsible for their care?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives with me at home and I'm responsible for him. I look after him full-time.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's clear - you're living with Alex and responsible for their care. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good progress! Now I need to ask about any other potential claimants:

**Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else applied to claim for Alex?**

In other words:
- Is there another person (such as Alex's other parent, grandparent, or guardian) who is also claiming or has claimed Child Benefit for Alex?
- If there is, have you and that person agreed who should be the main claimant?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after him, and nobody else has applied for it.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Where is Alex currently living?**

- **Living normally at home with you** (which seems to be the case based on what you've said)
- **In hospital** (for a stay)
- **In care** (residential care, children's home, etc.)
- **Fostered** (with foster carers)

I believe the answer is that Alex is living normally at home with you, but please confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex is living normally at home with me. He's not in hospital, care, or fostered or anything like that. Just living at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost there! Just one final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- Is the local council providing financial support towards Alex's care or accommodation?
- Or are you fully responsible for paying for Alex's upkeep yourself?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex's care or accommodation. I'm the one paying for everything - his food, clothes, housing, all of it. The council doesn't contribute anything.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's the final piece of information I need. Let me process your eligibility assessment now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! I have all the information I need. Now let me provide you with your eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **Great News! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit**

Based on your answers, **you qualify for Child Benefit for Alex**. Alex meets all the eligibility requirements!

### Summary of Why You're Eligible:

- ✅ **Age**: Alex is 3 years old (under 16)
- ✅ **Work**: Alex is not working
- ✅ **Benefits**: Alex is not receiving ESA or Universal Credit
- ✅ **Residency**: You normally live in the UK (Manchester)
- ✅ **Responsibility**: You live with Alex and are fully responsible for their care
- ✅ **No other claimants**: No one else is claiming for Alex
- ✅ **Living situation**: Alex lives normally at home with you
- ✅ **Financial support**: The council is not paying for Alex's accommodation

### Next Steps - How to Claim:

1. **Apply online** at [www.gov.uk/child-benefit](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim) or **by post using form CH2**

2. **You'll need to provide**:
   - Proof of identity for yourself (passport, driving licence, etc.)
   - Proof of identity for Alex (birth certificate or adoption certificate)
   - Your National Insurance number
   - Details of anyone else living in your household

3. **Payment**: Child Benefit is paid every 4 weeks directly into your bank account

4. **Important note**: If you or a partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may be subject to the **High Income Child Benefit Charge** - but you can still claim, and it's worth understanding how this works

### Useful Links:
- [How to claim Child Benefit](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim)
- [Child Benefit payment rates](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/rates)
- [High Income Child Benefit Charge](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/high-income-child-benefit-charge)

Congratulations! You should go ahead and make your claim. Good luck! 🎉
